root_cause.text: ep_remove() prematurely cleared file->f_ep to NULL while holding f_lock, allowing a concurrent __fput() to observe the transient NULL, skip eventpoll_release_file(), and free the file (and in the epoll-watches-epoll case, the watched struct eventpoll) while ep_remove() still operated on the freed objects (hlist_del_rcu and f_lock use).
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "ep_remove() (via ep_remove_file()) cleared file->f_ep under file->f_lock but then kept using @file inside the critical section... A concurrent __fput() taking the eventpoll_release() fastpath in that window observed the transient NULL, skipped eventpoll_release_file() and ran to f_op->release / file_free()." The patch fixes this by pinning the file via epi_fget() at the start of ep_remove() to prevent concurrent freeing.

A concurrent __fput() taking the eventpoll_release() fastpath in that window observed the transient NULL, skipped eventpoll_release_file() and ran to f_op->release / file_free()." candidates.rationale: Retrieves the file pointer that becomes invalid after concurrent __fput if file->f_ep is prematurely cleared.
Acquires f_lock that protects the clearing of file->f_ep, but the subsequent clearing while still holding this lock allows a concurrent __fput to observe the transient NULL and free the file.
This call is the direct location where file->f_ep is prematurely set to NULL while f_lock is held, enabling the race condition that leads to use-after-free.

In the nested epoll-watches-epoll case, this call (which likely contains hlist_del_rcu) operates on the epi that may already be freed if the watched eventpoll was freed by __fput triggered by the premature clear.
Although not directly causing the race, this call uses the file and could be reordered relative to the clear; it is part of the vulnerable sequence that occurs before the lock is taken.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call is the direct point where file->f_ep is prematurely set to NULL while f_lock is held, allowing a concurrent __fput() to observe the NULL, skip eventpoll_release_file(), and free the file (and potentially the watched eventpoll) before ep_remove() completes.

This call operates on epi after file->f_ep has been cleared and possibly after the file (and in nested epoll case, the watched eventpoll) has been freed, causing use-after-free when accessing epi in hlist_del_rcu or other operations.

This lock acquisition protects the clearing of file->f_ep, but the premature clear inside the locked section creates the window for a concurrent __fput() to see the NULL and free the file while ep_remove() still holds the lock and proceeds to use the file/epi.

This statement retrieves the file pointer early in ep_remove(). Although not directly causing the race, it is part of the vulnerable code path and the file pointer becomes invalid after the premature clear if the file is freed by __fput().

This statement executes before the f_lock is acquired and uses the file pointer. While it is not itself the vulnerable operation, it is part of the same function sequence and its execution is a prerequisite that leads to the vulnerable clear and subsequent use-after-free.
